validator: draft 1 has no hard problems. One soft problem: whatAmILookingAt is 15,236 characters, over the 12,000 guide.
research: The i8 research held four notes (Eaton's measured 1,200 V, the IMarEST damping line, ABB's filter to ground, MOTOR's latent first fault). Sixteen quotes already checked for the brief (notes 4.8, 4.1: Eaton's restrike chain from current zero to 2, 3 and 4 times and 'until some device fails'; Eaton's documented 480 V cases; IMarEST's kilohertz dielectric losses and 'just cannot occur'; ABB's 'disconnect EMC filter and ground-to-phase varistor'; Schneider's IEC 61800-3 cost and 'monitoring device compatible with nonlinear loads'; Bender's DC components; Cahier's capacitive leakages; GS38; MOTOR's chassis return path; Marine Insight's HV resistor) were appended to research.reply.txt as sources 71 to 87, with i8 notes, and run through sources.mjs (86 kept, 0 dropped). Three quotes over 40 words were cut to whole sentences first. The new sources (70 to 86 in research.json) and the i8 notes were merged into research.json; the hand-carried source 42 and the other ideas' notes were kept unchanged, as for i6 and i7.
keep: The idea is named up front: an arcing fault leaves charge on the capacitance, so the voltage to earth can climb in steps, damping limits it, and how far on ships is argued.

The causal chain is in words, one link a sentence: the burning arc is a solid fault (the shifted triangle); its current is charging current, which leads by 90 degrees, so it is zero at the voltage peak; the arc goes out there; the charge has no quick way off; L1 swings about the held star point to twice; a sudden restrike rings like a struck bell and overshoots; the arc goes out at the top of the ring.

Every figure recomputed: 440 / 1.732 = 254 V, x 1.414 = 359 V; held 1, 3, 5 times = 359, 1,077, 1,795 V and peaks 2, 4, 6 = 718, 1,436, 2,154 V with no losses; with half the ring, new held = 1.5 x P - H gives 1, 2, 2.5 (359, 718, 898 V) and peaks 2, 3, 3.5 (718, 1,077, 1,257 V), tending to 2 / (1 - 0.5) = 4; heavy losses 1 and 2 times; line-voltage peak 440 x 1.414 = 622 V; 3 x 377 x 1 uF x 254 = 287 mA, 2 uF 575 mA; 3 uF at 60 Hz = 884 ohm, 254 / sqrt(1000^2 + 884^2) = 190 mA (lesson 3's figure); 440 / 1000 = 440 mA.

The ladder reproduces the published chain exactly (2 times, the star point at 3, the phase at 4) and extends it with the same rule. The contested point is a picker, so both cases make sense on the picture and the text takes no side.

Each brief misconception has a DO screen: the arc going out resets the voltage (2), the held voltage taken as the peak (4), losses stopping any rise (6), the filter refitted to steady the monitor (8), a healthy monitor reading as safe to touch (10), the contest as who is right rather than what each case rests on (11), the filter's removal as free (12). Screen 9 shows the latent first fault making the system an earthed one.

It builds on, and does not repeat, lesson 3 (filters as capacitance, the 190 mA touch), lesson 5 (slower settling) and Electronics lesson 8 (filters out on IT): the new ground is why the filter comes out, what it costs, and the monitor that suits drives.

Twelve screens: SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (75 to 88 words) alternate with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, ending on three mixed puzzles 10 to 12. Each SHOW has a read sentence with no instruction to act. The View and Losses pickers and every readout row wrap on a phone.

faults.where: Screen 1 and explain jump from 'the arc goes out at a peak' to 'the star point is held 359 V' without saying that at that moment the shifted star point is a full peak from the hull. Explain's drive sentence says the filter ties the supply to earth but not why that matters (more first-fault current, a slower monitor).

'Only slow leakage can now drain the capacitance' (the monitor and other paths also bleed it). 'The drive then no longer meets its EMC standard' generalises one maker's statement about its product. 'The filter's capacitors protect nothing' (screen 12 hint). 'Every line of a healthy 440 V insulated supply sits 254 V from the hull' holds only with balanced insulation. Explain's 'the other lines sit 440 V from the hull' and screen 7's '575 mA' hold only for a solid fault.
The brief names the effect (peaks of 2 then 4 times) and the action, but not the cause, the star point held further out after each strike.

faults.note: taught mode, no checks. Each DO applies a rule to a new case: the held voltage plus the swing, a heavy-loss ladder worked from the rule, a monitor fault with the filter out, a healthy reading and a touch, what each side's case rests on, the price of removing the filter.
after the top-up, every step of the ladder, the documented 480 V cases, the marine damping case, the filter, its cost, the monitor and the touch limit carry a checked quote.
pickers and readouts wrap at 360 px; guide lines are labelled in words; no colour carries meaning on its own.
